name: Technical Demonstrator Architecture
consequences: Building non-production demonstrators validates platform-neutral authentication concepts but risks being dismissed as non-credible due to lack of real-world integration. This could delay policy traction unless demonstrator scope aligns with existing regulatory proof-of-concept expectations.
options: Develop a FIDO2/WebAuthn-based authentication flow using GrapheneOS to bypass platform-specific trust signals
Create a browser-based fallback mechanism leveraging hardware security modules independent of mobile OS integrity checks
Design a modular authentication framework that abstracts platform dependencies through open-standard attestation protocols
review: Prioritizing technical proof over policy alignment risks producing evidence that lacks procurement relevance, leaving institutional inertia unaddressed.

name: Policy Framing Strategy
consequences: Reframing dependency risks as resilience failures could shift decision-making priorities but may provoke backlash from stakeholders benefiting from the status quo. This requires careful calibration to avoid being labeled as anti-technology rather than pro-resilience.
options: Position platform neutrality as a critical infrastructure resilience requirement under national security frameworks
Frame supplier concentration risks using procurement compliance metrics tied to EU Digital Identity Wallet guidelines
Emphasize democratic accountability through transparency mandates for authentication trust model governance
review: Focusing on resilience metrics may neglect the technical complexities of implementing fallback paths, creating a gap between policy goals and engineering realities.

name: Coalition Engagement Model
consequences: Building cross-sector alliances strengthens advocacy power but risks diluting focus through conflicting stakeholder priorities. This requires maintaining technical credibility while navigating political trade-offs.
options: Form a technical-policy working group with civil society, academia, and public-sector continuity planners
Leverage privacy advocates to frame platform neutrality as a digital rights issue rather than a technical constraint
Create a vendor-agnostic consortium to jointly pressure AltID stakeholders through shared risk analysis
review: Over-reliance on coalition consensus may slow decision-making, leaving technical demonstration timelines vulnerable to political delays.

name: Procurement Requirement Influence
consequences: Influencing AltID procurement standards could institutionalize platform neutrality but faces resistance from existing vendors. This requires aligning technical evidence with procurement compliance frameworks.
options: Embed fallback authentication requirements in AltID's technical specifications through formal feedback loops

Leverage EU-wide digital identity working groups to standardize fallback access requirements across member states
review: Focusing on procurement language may overlook the technical challenges of retrofitting existing systems, creating a gap between policy goals and implementation feasibility.

Develop hardware-token-based authentication workflows compatible with GrapheneOS and other privacy-focused platforms
Pilot decentralized identity protocols using blockchain-anchored verifiable credentials for critical services
review: Diversifying authentication paths enhances security but increases user complexity, leaving the gap of ensuring seamless integration with existing systems.
